documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Initiative
documents.summary: The Provost's AI Initiative page describes the university's AI goals and offers optional syllabus language. The language lets instructors decide, requires documentation of any AI use, treats undocumented use as plagiarism and tells students to assume AI is disallowed if the syllabus is silent.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule: AI uses are "as determined by the instructor of the course" and faculty are "encouraged (but not required)" to adopt the suggested language, so the decision is delegated. The silent-syllabus default ("assume ... disallowed") is a fallback inside that delegation, not a blanket ban.

units.why: The page opens with the initiative purpose, "to leverage AI for student success", which sets the institution-level aim and scope for AI use, so it is a framework statement (P56) that only informs.
units.anchor: Its primary goal is to leverage AI for student success.

units.why: The committee "use AI to facilitate student learning, identify at-risk students earlier and increase student retention", an institutional purpose statement; P56 fits better than P55 because it states aims, not evidence collection.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Guide: Faculty and Staff Information
documents.summary: The Faculty and Staff Guide section on AI tells instructors to be clear about acceptable AI use, which they decide, and to consider differing rules by project. It restates that AI use must be documented, that undocumented use is plagiarism and that students should assume AI is disallowed when no guidance exists.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "The instructor of the course determines legitimate uses" and tells faculty to "be clear" and "differentiate" across projects, so the stance is delegated. The default-disallowed line is only a fallback for silent courses.

documents.unit: Research Integrity and Compliance (Academic Integrity Guide)
documents.title: Academic Integrity Guide: Student Information
documents.summary: The Student Guide's AI section tells students that rules differ by course and instructor, that they should talk to the instructor first and document all AI use, and that undocumented use is plagiarism. If no AI guidance is given they should assume AI is not allowed, and they are responsible for what they submit.
documents.stance_why: The section says AI "may be allowed in some courses ... prohibited by others" and tells students to follow "your instructors' guidelines", so instructors decide. The "assume ... not allowed" line applies only when guidance is missing.

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found. All three documents are university-level and share the same core AI text (instructor decides; document use; undocumented use is plagiarism; assume disallowed if silent; students responsible). Generic academic-integrity content (group work, misconduct definitions, reporting, meeting the student, sanctions, appeal) was not coded because it is not AI-specific.
